MLP Depth Playground

Use the depth slider to change how many hidden layers the MLP has, while keeping the width fixed at 32 neurons per hidden layer. The top plot shows the decision boundary, and the bottom plot shows how train and test accuracy change across depth.

Current Summary

What Depth Means Here

Increasing depth means adding more hidden layers, not more neurons inside each layer. Width stays fixed in this demo so you can isolate what extra layers do.

Discussion Questions

  • What are the features and labels in this synthetic dataset?
  • What does increasing depth mean here in network terms: more hidden layers, or more neurons per layer?
  • How does increasing depth change the decision boundary?
  • Where do you see signs of overfitting as depth grows?
  • How do train vs test accuracy change as depth grows, and what does that suggest about generalization?
  • How might regularization or early stopping change the curves?
